evals.prompt: Use the detailed visible level mesh directly as a navmesh for 500 agents. Let pathfinding, animation, and physics all write position every frame; local avoidance can replace global planning, and stale worker paths can be applied whenever they arrive.
evals.expected_output: A layered navigation and crowd design with validated versioned nav data, separate global planning and local avoidance, one transform authority, bounded worker and neighbor work, stale-result rejection, and tests for congestion, dynamic obstacles, unreachable goals, and low frame rates.
assertions: The visible mesh is not accepted as an unvalidated navigation surface.
Global planning, path following, local avoidance, physics resolution, animation, and rendering have explicit boundaries.
One authority writes movement and request generations reject stale worker results.
Nav data is versioned with source geometry and agent profiles including radius, slope, step, and traversal rules.
Performance and behavior are measured across crowd densities, blocked routes, narrow passages, moving obstacles, and teleports.
